theoremDRRes_issues: Setup (INV-reduction l.19-20) is correct. F, R >= 1 by proof-DR l.26-28. F >= 2 because F = 1 gives R = 4p-2 >= 3p-1, so Lemma EGZ applies. (E) follows from Lemma EGZ, which holds for any N (partial l.27-28).

(P) is correct, but r_i is never defined in Sec. 1; it should be r_i = a_i + b_i = |R_i|. In the cyclic gap model (partial l.17-19), the gap ending at the first letter of S_i has n_t = r_i and the other l_i - 1 gaps of S_i are empty. So sum_t floor(n_t/2) = sum_i floor(r_i/2), and Theorem P (N = 4p-1 <= 4p-1) gives F + sum_i floor(r_i/2) <= 3p-2.

(V) is correct but the choice of I is not written out. Take I = every second interior gap of each reflection run. S_j has l_j - 1 consecutive empty interior gaps, of which ceil((l_j-1)/2) = floor(l_j/2) are pairwise non-adjacent. Interior gaps of different runs are separated by the non-empty gap holding a rotation run, so I is cyclically non-adjacent and |I| = H. Each bracket item is (2,0) because y_{t-1} = y_t. Since the I-gaps are empty, all R rotations lie outside them, so the item count is H + R. Davenport-alpha's own hypothesis F >= 2 holds, and size < 4p holds because N = 4p-1. So R + H <= 3p-2.

(Pairs) is correct. If H >= p, choose c_j <= floor(l_j/2) with sum c_j = p and select 2c_j letters from each S_j and no rotations. The product is a product of blocks sigma_{y_j}^{2c_j}, each equal to 1. Even a run that wraps around the linear cut gives sigma^alpha * 1 * sigma^beta = 1, so no cyclic issue arises. 'Each pair adjacent in the selection' is more than is needed.

(D0) is correct. Each rotation run lies inside one gap. If a_i >= p (or b_i >= p), take K = p equal rotations, which sum to p*(+-1) = 0. This satisfies Doubling with j = 0: a one-gap stretch, no M-gaps, |K| = p, N = 4p-1, F >= 1.

Monotonicity holds only for deleting a letter from a run of length >= 2, which is the deletion proof-DR l.29-31 uses. 'Deleting a letter inside a run' / 'in-run deletion' is not defined in Sec. 1. Deleting a run of length 1 merges its neighbours, and then floor((l+l')/2), floor((r+r')/2), a_i and b_i can go up. With the correct definition, R, F + sum floor(r_i/2), R + H, H, a_i and b_i are all non-increasing. The 2k runs, k, F, R >= 1, membership in RGR and avoidance all survive, so w' is an inherited avoider in RGR_{4p-2}(p) with the same k.

Uses of INV in proof-DR: only at (i), applied to the deletions from X and from Y (parity) and to the deletion from X (k <= p). (ii) and (iii) use sigma_y^{2p} and Doubling on w itself. So INV_Res is enough. Remark: (Pairs) and (D0) for w already give |X| <= 2p-1 for a reflection run and <= 2p-2 for a rotation run, so the one-long-run case forces k >= p+1 and k <= p rules it out directly.

Remark, not an error: (E) follows from (V). For any avoider in RGR_{4p-2}(p) with F, R >= 1, conditions (E), (P), (V) and (Pairs) hold automatically: EGZ and Pairs work for any N, Theorem P for N <= 4p-1, and Davenport-alpha needs size < 4p and F >= 2, where F = 1 would give R = 4p-3 >= 3p-1. Only (D0) is a real restriction, because Doubling needs N = 4p-1. Equivalently, INV_Res(p) is INV(p) restricted to avoiders with all a_i, b_i <= p-1.
lemma_statements_issues: INV_Res(p) is equivalent to RUNS(p) together with PAR(p) as stated (PAR only for k <= p), since (for all w': A and B) is the same as (for all w': A) and (for all w': A implies B). So the pair is exactly the hypothesis of DR-Res.

Both lemmas are actually used, in the right order. RUNS comes first, applied to any in-run deletion; one exists because 4p-1 is odd and 2k is even. It gives k <= p for w (same k) and rules out the one-long-run configuration, which has k >= p+1 under (Pairs)/(D0). PAR is then applied to the deletions from X and from Y, ruling out two long runs.

proof-DR's text (l.32-35) uses parity before it derives k <= p. With PAR conditional on k <= p, the proof has to be reordered so RUNS comes first. The bracket note at l.37-38 says this, but tersely: 'if k > p no parity statement is needed' really means 'k > p contradicts RUNS'. It should spell out the reordered steps.
Strictly, DR-Res uses PAR and RUNS only on in-run deletions of RGR avoiders of length 4p-1, which is a subclass of inherited avoiders, so weaker statements would suffice. This is not an error.
evidence_wording_issues: The framing is mostly sound. The headers say 'aids, not proofs' and 'finite-exact aids', the results are stated per prime, 'none' is described as uncertified rather than as an avoider, and Sec. 4 says PAR and RUNS are open for general p.

Sec. 3 l.55-56: 'k > p cases are uncertified by Phi <= 2 at p = 5' overgeneralises. k = 6 > p is certified (l.49 gives 'k <= 6: none = 0'; Sec. 3.1 l.70 lists only k = 7, 8, 9). It should say 'some k > p cases (k = 7, 8, 9)'.

Sec. 3.1 l.73-76, labelled 'exact, from Lemma GR', is wrong. C = Phi, C_max = Phi and 'all but Phi-1 rotations selected' are correct, and so is the q-range if q counts the unselected effectively-positive rotations. But with Lemma GR's t = A+ - A-, the achievable values are t = D(z) + (Phi-1) - 2q, which is every even integer in an interval (step 2, which is exactly Ach(z)). The stated t = D(z) + 2(Phi-1) - 4q is always odd, because D(z) is a sum of 2p-1 terms +-1, so it is never achievable. 'Difference 4' is wrong here, and so is 'step-4 progressions' in Sec. 4(b). Check with p = 3, all e_i = +1, z = (+,+,+,-,-): the true t values are {0, 2}; the formula gives {3, -1}.

Same passage: 't = sum_{i in P} theta_i' should be a congruence mod p, and theta_i and P are never defined in this file (from Lemma GR, theta_i = y_i - y_{i-1} and P is the Minus set). The passage is a derived mathematical claim, not computational evidence, so it needs either a proof or a label saying it has not been checked.
Sec. 3.1 l.60 says 'sha256 recorded in Sec. 4', but Sec. 4 has no hash. The provenance pointer leads nowhere, and Sec. 3 l.42 cites the code with no hash or run log either.

'PAR(5) and PAR(7) hold' (l.65) and 'RUNS(5), RUNS(7) hold' (l.77) are computer-dependent finite results. They should carry an [F] tag inline, as proof-DR does. Sec. 4(a) states 'joint certificates are forced-difference contradictions ... not additive when a run is even' as a general fact, but no data or proof is given; it should be framed as an observation at p = 5 and 7.

Sec. 1: write out the Davenport-alpha set I: every second interior gap of each reflection run, |I| = H, cyclic non-adjacency guaranteed by the rotation gaps between runs, all R rotations outside the I-gaps, item count R + H, and size < 4p because N = 4p-1.

notes:
Only ./input was read. The code and novelty were not assessed.

(1) Theorem DR-Res is correct. All five conditions follow from the cited lemmas at N = 4p-1. Davenport-alpha's own hypothesis F >= 2 is established. Theorem P's n_t specialises to the rotation-run lengths r_i, and Davenport-alpha's item count becomes H + R. The pairs selection gives identity blocks. Doubling with j = 0 applies to p equal rotations in one gap. All quantities are non-increasing under deletion from a run of length >= 2, and proof-DR applies INV only to such deletions. The fixes are wording only: r_i undefined, 'in-run deletion' undefined, and the Davenport-alpha set I not written out.

(2) PAR (for k <= p) together with RUNS is logically equivalent to INV_Res. Both are used, RUNS first. The text should make the reordering of proof-DR explicit.

(3) The finite results are framed as aids and not overclaimed for general p, with these exceptions:
- one overgeneralisation ('k > p cases are uncertified');
- a dangling sha256 pointer;
- a genuine factor-2 error in the 'exact' formula for the fully alternating words (step 4 should be step 2), repeated in Sec. 4(b). It does not affect DR-Res or the lemma statements, but any RUNS attack built on the step-4 formula would be wrong.

Remark: among avoiders of length 4p-2, only (D0) is a real restriction, so INV_Res = INV restricted to words with all a_i, b_i <= p-1.
